_readme.what: Balance measurements enabled by mapstudy.balance's new `characters` argument (see mapstudy/balance.py, protocol_key/rollout/evaluate/evaluate_many): first, character_3 (wall/dash) against the study E suite; then a role-swapped-kits condition added to test what was actually driving character3_both's result -- the tagger role, or whichever role holds the cc/engage ability pair.
_readme.stage: report (n=240, round_time=120.0) -- confirmed, not a search-stage estimate. A quick n=24 pass ran first and pointed the same direction; this is the number that counts.
_readme.rules: RULES_V2 (fractional 0.6 required_generators / 0.75 active_exits, random_spawns=True, late_exits=False) -- the same rule set every other number in this study is measured under.
_readme.policies: ChasePolicy (tagger) vs FleePolicy (runner), both frozen heuristics, same as every other balance number here.

conditions.shipped_kits_on: control -- the shipped tagger/runner pairing (character_2/character_1: stasis+destiny vs journey+rewind), AS-DESIGNED constants (no PLAYABLE_TUNING/BALANCED_TUNING applied). Reproduces the as-designed number from docs/skill-balance.md (~0.360 at n=240 over this suite) within sampling noise.
conditions.character3_both: test -- BOTH roles play character_3 (wall+dash) instead of their shipped kit, also AS-DESIGNED constants (WALL_DURATION=6.0, WALL_COOLDOWN=15.0, DASH_DISTANCE=1.5, DASH_DURATION=0.15, DASH_COOLDOWN=10.0 -- no tuning surface has been fit for this kit yet).
conditions.swapped_kits_on: test -- role-swapped shipped kits: tagger plays character_1 (journey+rewind), runner plays character_2 (stasis+destiny) -- the mirror image of the shipped assignment. Added to separate 'role' from 'ability category' as the driver of the tagger-favoring shift seen in shipped_kits_on: does the tagger win because it is the tagger, or because it holds the cc/engage pair? Also AS-DESIGNED constants. Same caveat as character3_both: neither ChasePolicy nor FleePolicy has a kit it has bespoke tactics for here (stasis/destiny native logic is ChasePolicy's, journey/rewind native logic is FleePolicy's; each is now playing the other's off-kit pair), so both run purely on the generic ABILITY_TAGS fallback -- directly comparable to character3_both on that axis.

headline.note: Whoever holds the cc/engage pair (stasis+destiny) wins more, not 'the tagger role wins more': mean runner WR is 0.128 when the tagger holds it (shipped_kits_on), 0.348 with nobody holding any pair (skills_off), 0.376 with neither role holding a cc/engage pair (character3_both, both play wall+dash), and 0.501 -- almost exactly even -- when the RUNNER holds stasis+destiny (swapped_kits_on). character3_both's earlier 'better than both controls' result is therefore better read as 'removing the tagger's cc/engage tool removes its biggest lever' rather than 'wall/dash is well-designed' -- see caveats.

caveats: ChasePolicy/FleePolicy have no bespoke tactics for wall or dash (unlike stasis/destiny/journey/rewind, which each have tuned native logic). Both abilities are only driven by the generic ABILITY_TAGS fallback in tag_game/agents.py:_generic_ability, which exists to make an off-kit ability get pressed at all, not to be a tuned opponent for it. These numbers may move, in either direction, once character_3 gets logic like the other four abilities did.

Atrium is the worst map under every condition tested here (skills off included), so its character3_both error (0.308) likely reflects the map's existing tagger-favoring geometry more than the new kit.
Only the symmetric case (both roles on character_3) was measured. character_3 vs a shipped-kit opponent was not.

swapped_kits_on's mean WR (0.501) is close to even only in aggregate: per-map it is NOT uniformly balanced. Only Twins (err 0.013) is statistically indistinguishable from balanced (1/7, vs character3_both's 3/7); Lv3/Loops/Spiral/Foundry overshoot toward the runner (wr 0.57-0.68) while Warren/Atrium still favor the tagger. The low mean|err| (0.135) is a mix of opposite-direction misses, not most maps individually near 0.5 -- see aggregate()'s own warning against reading mean win rate as balance.
_readme.produced_by: ad hoc script using mapstudy.balance.evaluate with pool=multiprocessing.Pool(8), cache=default_cache() -- not scripts/skill_sweep.py, which does not know about `characters` yet.
